notes.text: Support Django projects with the same managed worktree switching, reservations, monitoring, logs, GUI, and MCP workflow as Next.js projects.

notes.author: agent:codex
notes.text: Most controller behavior is already framework-independent. The main architectural change is resolving a typed launch adapter for the selected worktree at every start, because a Django interpreter may live inside that worktree rather than at one path captured during registration.

problem: Project registration currently requires package.json and a Node.js dev script. Django repositories therefore cannot use the controller's stable ports, worktree switching, reservations, resource monitoring, logs, or MCP lifecycle tools without bypassing Worktree Switcher.

risk.rollback: Disable Django registration and retain the existing Node.js launch resolver. Removing the adapter must not alter Django repositories, virtual environments, databases, uploads, or generated files.

scope: Introduce a persisted runtime kind and a typed launch-adapter boundary instead of adding Django branches to the Node.js resolver. Preserve existing Node.js and Next.js behavior through their own adapter.
Resolve the launch command against the exact Git-discovered worktree on every start or switch. Do not persist an executable path derived from one worktree and reuse it blindly for another.

Detect Django without executing repository code, initially from a regular manage.py file and optionally corroborating pyproject.toml or requirements files. Allow an explicit human selection when detection is ambiguous.

Resolve Python without shell activation, preferring an executable selected worktree/.venv/bin/python, then selected worktree/venv/bin/python, then an explicitly approved interpreter path, with an actionable failure when none is usable.

Start development mode with a shell-free argument array equivalent to python manage.py runserver 0.0.0.0:{port}. Keep host and port controller-owned so environment profiles or MCP input cannot redirect the managed listener.

Integrate Django settings, working directories, environment files, and non-secret or referenced-secret variables through FEAT-20260829-launch-environment-profiles rather than accepting free-form shell commands.

Reuse the existing process ownership, capacity, reservation, bounded logs, resource monitoring, and TCP readiness mechanisms. Add human-readable failures for missing manage.py, interpreter, Django module, settings imports, occupied ports, and early process exit; never run migrations automatically.

Expose detected runtime kind, interpreter source, effective redacted configuration, and runtime diagnostics in the dashboard and read-only MCP status. Existing claim, start, switch, renew, and release tools must work without framework-specific variants; configuration mutations remain capability-gated and audited.

Extend worktree storage visibility with allowlisted Python cache categories. Any cleanup must require a stopped and unreserved worktree, reject symlinks and canonical-path escape, and never remove virtual environments, migrations, SQLite databases, collected static files, media, uploads, or dependency directories.

Keep Gunicorn, Uvicorn, Daphne, ASGI/WSGI production profiles, automatic dependency installation, virtual-environment creation, migrations, and controller-managed Django HTTPS outside the initial development-server adapter. Track production serving separately after the development workflow is validated.
title: Manage Django development servers through runtime adapters
validation: Register a Django repository, start its selected worktree, and verify the managed process listens on the stable configured LAN port while status, logs, CPU, RAM, and process count remain available.

Switch between two Django worktrees with different project-local virtual-environment paths and verify each launch resolves its own interpreter without starting a duplicate server or reusing the previous worktree's executable.

Verify missing manage.py, missing or non-executable Python, missing Django, settings import failure, occupied port, and startup timeout each produce a useful operator-facing error without leaking environment values.
Verify reservations and global server capacity apply identically to Django and Node.js projects through both the dashboard and existing MCP lifecycle tools.
Verify detection never imports or executes managed repository code and launch remains shell-free even when paths or settings contain spaces or shell metacharacters.
Verify Python cache cleanup cannot follow symlinks or delete .venv, venv, migrations, db.sqlite3, static output, media, uploads, source files, or paths outside the selected Git-discovered worktree.
Verify all existing Node.js and Next.js launch, TLS, switching, and cache-reset tests remain unchanged and pass after introducing the adapter boundary.
value: Django developers and coding agents can share the same bounded local control plane as Next.js projects without ad hoc server commands, port conflicts, or framework-specific MCP workflows.
